content: 1. Martinez-Dominguez SJ, Lajusticia H, Chedraui P, and Perez-Lopez FR conducted a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials to evaluate the impact of structured exercise programs on anxiety symptoms in middle-aged and older women. Their findings were published in Climacteric in 2018. 2. Patterson R, McNamara E, Tainio M, de Sa TH, Smith AD, Sharp SJ, and colleagues systematically reviewed the relationship between sedentary behavior and the risk of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular mortality, cancer mortality, and the incidence of type 2 diabetes. Their dose-response meta-analysis was published in European Journal of Epidemiology in 2018. 3. Bailey DP, Hewson DJ, Champion RB, and Sayegh SM performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to assess the association between sitting time and the risk of cardiovascular disease and diabetes. Their work was published in American Journal of Preventive Medicine in 2019. 4. Ahmad S, Shanmugasegaram S, Walker KL, and Prince SA examined sedentary time as a risk factor for cardiometabolic diseases and their biomarkers in South Asian adults. Their systematic review was published in International Journal of Public Health in 2017. 5. Mahmood S, MacInnis RJ, English DR, Karahalios A, and Lynch BM investigated the relationship between domain-specific physical activity, sedentary behavior, and the risk of colon and rectal cancer. Their systematic review and meta-analysis were published in International Journal of Epidemiology in 2017. 6. Berger FF, Leitzmann MF, Hillreiner A, Sedlmeier AM, Prokopidi-Danisch ME, Burger M, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohort studies to explore the association between sedentary behavior and prostate cancer. Their findings were published in Cancer Prevention Research in 2019. 7. Chan DSM, Abar L, Cariolou M, Nanu N, Greenwood DC, Bandera EV, and colleagues, as part of the World Cancer Research Fund International Continuous Update Project, systematically reviewed observational cohort studies to assess the impact of physical activity, sedentary behavior, adiposity, and weight change on breast cancer risk. Their meta-analysis was published in Cancer Causes & Control in 2019. 8. Wang J, Huang L, Gao Y, Wang Y, Chen S, Huang J, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of observational studies, finding that physically active individuals have a 23% lower risk of any colorectal neoplasia and a 27% lower risk of advanced colorectal neoplasia compared to inactive individuals. Their study was published in British Journal of Sports Medicine in 2019. 9. Bueno de Souza RO, Marcon LF, Arruda ASF, Pontes Junior FL, and Melo RC evaluated the effects of mat Pilates on the physical functional performance of older adults through a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Their findings were published in American Journal of Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation in 2018. 10. Sherrington C, Fairhall N, Kwok W, Wallbank G, Tiedemann A, Michaleff Z, and colleagues systematically reviewed evidence on physical activity and fall prevention in individuals aged 65 years and older to inform WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behavior. Their work is in press in Journal of Physical Activity and Health. 11. Da Rosa Orssatto LB, de la Rocha Freitas C, Shield AJ, Silveira Pinto R, and Trajano GS examined the effects of resistance training concentric velocity on the functional capacity of older adults. Their systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials were published in Experimental Gerontology in 2019. 12. Du MC, Ouyang YQ, Nie XF, Huang Y, and Redding SR conducted a meta-analysis to evaluate the effects of physical exercise during pregnancy on maternal and infant outcomes in overweight and obese pregnant women. Their findings were published in Birth in 2019. 13. Beetham KS, Giles C, Noetel M, Clifton V, Jones JC, and Naughton G systematically reviewed the effects of vigorous-intensity exercise during the third trimester of pregnancy. Their meta-analysis was published in BMC Pregnancy and Childbirth in 2019. 14. Nakamura A, van der Waerden J, Melchior M, Bolze C, El-Khoury F, and Pryor L systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed the relationship between physical activity during pregnancy and postpartum depression. Their findings were published in Journal of Affective Disorders. 15. Mijatovic-Vukas J, Capling L, Cheng S, Stamatakis E, Louie J, Cheung NW, and colleagues systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed the associations of diet and physical activity with the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus. Their study was published in Nutrients in 2018. 16. Schmitz KH, Campbell AM, Stuiver MM, Pinto BM, Schwartz AL, Morris GS, and colleagues emphasized the role of exercise as medicine in oncology, advocating for clinician engagement to help patients maintain physical activity during cancer treatment. Their work was published in CA: A Cancer Journal for Clinicians in 2019. 17. Colberg SR, Sigal RJ, Yardley JE, Riddell MC, Dunstan DW, Dempsey PC, and colleagues published a position statement on physical activity and exercise for diabetes management in Diabetes Care in 2016. 18. Whelton PK, Carey RM, Aronow WS, Casey DE Jr., Collins KJ, Dennison Himmelfarb C, and colleagues developed the 2017 ACC/AHA guidelines for the prevention, detection, evaluation, and management of high blood pressure in adults. Their report was published in Hypertension in 2018. 19. The Swedish National Institute of Public Health published a comprehensive report on the role of physical activity in the prevention and treatment of diseases in 2010. 20. Friedenreich CM, Stone CR, Cheung WY, and Hayes SC systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed the impact of physical activity on mortality in cancer survivors. Their findings were published in JNCI Cancer Spectrum in 2019. 21. Costa EC, Hay JL, Kehler DS, Boreskie KF, Arora RC, Umpierre D, and colleagues compared the effects of high-intensity interval training versus moderate-intensity continuous training on blood pressure in adults with pre-hypertension or established hypertension. Their meta-analysis was published in Sports Medicine in 2018. 22. Liu Y, Ye W, Chen Q, Zhang Y, Kuo CH, and Korivi M systematically reviewed and meta-analyzed the relationship between resistance exercise intensity and improvements in HbA1c and insulin levels in patients with type 2 diabetes. Their study was published in International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health in 2019. 23. The WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behavior were developed with input from experts in physical activity, adolescent health, aging, disability, mental health, injury prevention, cancer, pregnancy, and surveillance. These guidelines aim to provide evidence-based recommendations for improving global health outcomes.
